name: Parfum Satori
about: A one-perfumer house run by a French-trained Japanese nose who works almost entirely from Japanese plants, tea, incense culture and seasonal moods.
why: Barely distributed outside Japan, so it is still a discovery for most Western noses. One of the clearest examples of a modern Japanese perfume voice.

sig.name: SATORI (Eau de Parfum)
sig.profile: Imagine the calm of a temple incense ceremony, then add a thread of cocoa and cinnamon. It is built to suggest kyara, the rarest grade of agarwood, without the barnyard heaviness some oud carries: dry, quiet, warm and very straight-lined on skin.

name: SHIRO
about: A Japanese skincare-and-fragrance brand known for soft, clean, everyday scents sold at very gentle prices.
why: Hugely popular inside Japan but little known abroad. The easiest, cheapest way to try the Japanese taste for clean, close-to-skin scent.

sig.name: White Tea Eau de Parfum
sig.profile: Fresh-cut citrus over a cup of green tea, finishing like clean laundry. Light, polite and office-safe; the brand says it lasts about five to six hours.

price.note: Page did not say whether tax is included. Was sold out on the check date.

name: J-Scent
about: A Japanese line that turns everyday Japanese moments (sake, tatami, ramune soda, wet streets) into wearable perfumes.
why: Playful and very place-specific, a good bridge between Japanese culture and Western perfume formats.

sig.name: Hanamizake
sig.profile: Cherry blossom drifting into a cup of chilled sake: a fruity, rice-wine sweetness on top, then soft spring florals and a clean woody musk. Bright and springlike.

price.note: Canadian price from an overseas reseller; it costs much less in Japan.

name: Shoyeido
about: A centuries-old Kyoto incense maker. Not perfume in a bottle, but the root of how Japan thinks about scent (the art of kōdō, 'listening' to incense).
why: Incense is the original Asian perfume. Useful for Clay as a room-and-ritual layer, and a cheap way to learn notes like sandalwood, agarwood and clove.

sig.name: Kyonishiki (Autumn Leaves) incense
sig.profile: Cinnamon and sandalwood smoke meant to recall autumn in Kyoto's Arashiyama hills: warm, spiced and soothing rather than churchy.

price.note: Starting price for the smallest bundle (incense sticks, not ml). Sold out on the check date.

name: Tamburins
about: A Seoul design-led beauty brand from the team behind the eyewear label Gentle Monster. Famous for sculptural stores and egg-shaped perfume bottles.
why: Defines the 'K-scent' look: soft, skin-like, slightly herbal, with art-gallery packaging.

sig.name: Perfume CHAMO
sig.profile: Chamomile tea with a spoon of honey, sharpened by a slightly bitter sage, then settling into pale wood and warm musk. Cozy and calming.

price.note: 11 ml and 14 ml egg sizes also sold.

name: Nonfiction
about: A Korean fragrance-and-body brand known for warm, wearable 'skin scents' and a strong cult following across Asia.
why: Shows the Korean move from sweet to grown-up woods and tobacco, at prices well below Western niche.

sig.name: In The Shower
sig.profile: A bitter-orange aperitif poured over smoky tobacco and dry wood. Despite the name it is warm and moody rather than soapy.

price.note: Price reported by a Singapore beauty site; bottle size not given.

name: GRANHAND.
about: A Seoul perfumery with apothecary-style shops, making perfumes, multi-use sprays and scented goods.
why: Very affordable Korean niche with an English store, good for building a first 'Korean shelf'.

sig.name: Marine Orchid (Multi Perfume)
sig.profile: Juicy pear and mandarin over a soft bouquet, finished with a hint of toffee. Sweet but airy; the 'multi perfume' format is meant for skin, fabric and rooms.

price.note: Price shown for the Susie Salmon Multi Perfume 100 ml; the multi perfumes share this format.

name: BORNTOSTANDOUT (BTSO)
about: A bold Seoul house with dramatic, cocktail-like concepts that has started to appear in Western niche shops.
why: The most 'loud' Korean house, a counterpoint to the soft K-scent stereotype.

sig.name: Mad Honey
sig.profile: Rum-soaked honey and rose over thick vanilla and resin. Rich, sticky-sweet and long-lasting; best for cold evenings.

price.note: Bottle size not given in the source.

name: Pesade
about: A small Korean label with an English shop and very low entry prices.
why: One of the cheapest ways to sample Korean indie perfume.

sig.name: Mid Mountain
sig.profile: A clean lemon-and-flowers opening on a soft cedar and musk base. Easy, fresh and versatile.

price.note: Reported price, possibly a sale price; size not given.

name: To Summer (观夏)
about: One of the brands leading China's new 'Eastern' perfume wave, built on tea, osmanthus, magnolia and quiet botanical moods.
why: Chinese niche is the fastest-growing scene in Asia and still almost unknown in Canada. This house is the most approachable entry point and ships internationally.

sig.name: Osmanthus Perfume
sig.profile: Osmanthus is the apricot-and-suede flower that scents Chinese autumns. Here it is juicy and peachy at first, then settles into a soft, clean amber. Also see their Triple Tea, a dry, unsweetened mix of green, black and rock tea.

price.note: 30 ml US$139.90, 100 ml US$279.90 (read from the shop data). Was sold out on the check date.

name: DOCUMENTS (闻献)
about: A Shanghai house started around 2020, known for dark, concentrated perfumes, incense and tea themes, and gallery-like stores. Its themes lean on Chinese materials and Zen calm.
why: Considered the most avant-garde of the new Chinese houses. Mostly sold in China (Taobao/Tmall), so it is truly untapped here.

sig.name: Naive (初熟之物)
sig.profile: The house style: a numbing tingle of Sichuan pepper and bright citrus, then incense smoke, tea and cedar on a resinous, musky base. Meditative and bold at once. (Notes listed are the house's typical palette, not one confirmed formula.)

price.note: No public English price list; check their Taobao or Tmall store.

name: Uttori
about: A Chinese artisan house that reworks familiar Chinese plants, tea and gardens into modern perfumes.
why: Small, story-led and still rare outside China.

sig.name: Moss Rock (苔庭)
sig.profile: Named after a moss garden but softer than it sounds: creamy coconut and pear with tropical white flowers over a soft vanilla wood. Gentle and comforting.

price.note: Price not published in English sources.

name: ICHUN
about: A small Taiwanese perfumer (sold through the YANYANTANG aroma shop) whose scents come from childhood memories of Taiwanese temples and hometown flowers.
why: Taiwan's indie scene is tiny and almost invisible abroad. Temple-inspired perfume is a scent story you won't find in Western lines.

sig.name: Prayer (初一十五)
sig.profile: A visit to a Taiwanese temple on the 1st and 15th of the lunar month, without the heavy smoke: pink pepper stands in for incense sparks, then rose and a warm agarwood-sandalwood base.

name: Bombay Perfumery
about: A modern Mumbai house that tells Indian city and travel stories with Western-style eaux de parfum, many using Indian materials.
why: Modern India in a bottle, at mid prices, with a global store that ships.

sig.name: Chai Musk
sig.profile: A railway-station cup of masala chai: ginger and lemongrass steam, toasted nuts, then a milky, slightly smoky sandalwood. Warm and comforting. Their Seven Islands is the beachy alternative.

name: Gulab Singh Johrimal
about: Delhi's oldest perfumery, run by the same family since 1816. Makes ittars (attars): plant oils distilled the old way into a sandalwood-oil base, plus pure 'ruh' (the first, purest distillate of a flower).
why: Attars are alcohol-free, very concentrated, and almost unknown to Western shoppers. Ruh Gulab (rose) here is among the most respected anywhere.

sig.name: Ruh Gulab (pure rose distillate)
sig.profile: Rose the way the petals smell, not perfume-counter rose: green, honeyed and almost fruity, worn as a drop of oil. Also look for khus (vetiver root), cooling and earthy, and their sandalwood blends.

price.note: Owner's stated range per 10 ml: blended perfumes from about ₹100, pure Ruh Gulab up to ₹28,000. Their own shop sells discovery sets from about ₹1,065 to ₹2,005.

name: Spa Ceylon
about: A Sri Lankan Ayurveda-inspired wellness brand whose perfumes are named after island places: Kandy, Mirissa, Arugam Bay.
why: Sri Lankan scent stories (temple flowers, spice gardens, surf towns) at accessible prices.

sig.name: Kandyan Rose Eau de Perfume
sig.profile: A sugared rose garden: berry-bright rose and jasmine on a candy-soft vanilla base, inspired by the royal flower gardens of old Kandy.

name: Karmakamet
about: A Bangkok scent house in apothecary style, known for perfume oils, solid perfumes and its 'Scentorium', a free walk-through museum of hundreds of smells.
why: Thai scent culture (tea houses, jasmine garlands, Chinese-Thai apothecaries) in oil and balm forms that are rare in the West.

sig.name: Authentic Perfume Body Oil (blends)
sig.profile: Concentrated body oils in blends with names like Tea Chamber, Hainan, Garden Breath and White Space. Oils sit closer to skin than sprays and last well in heat. (Notes per blend are listed on the site.)

name: HMNS
about: One of the brands behind Indonesia's local-perfume boom (pronounced 'humans'), with bold names and earthy, spicy, sweet scents at friendly prices.
why: Indonesia is the source of patchouli, vetiver and clove for the whole perfume world, and its local brands are only now getting noticed.

sig.name: ORGSM Eau de Parfum
sig.profile: Crisp red apple opening onto the three classic flowers (rose, jasmine, peony), then a warm vanilla-amber finish. A sweet, flirty floral and the brand's best known scent.

price.note: Read from the shop's product data (Rupiah).

name: TADHANA
about: A Filipino niche house by ISIPCA-trained perfumer Shale Albao, built on Philippine materials like sampaguita, calamansi, dalandan, almaciga resin and Davao coffee. Prices are in Canadian dollars.
why: A Filipino house with a Toronto link, so shipping and pricing are friendly for Canada. A rare chance to smell Philippine raw materials in fine perfume.

sig.name: Rockstar
sig.profile: Ripe mango and dalandan (a green Philippine orange) with coconut water and creamy island flowers, grounded by vetiver and a touch of agarwood. Sunny but not cheap-smelling.

price.note: 10 ml travel size C$60.

name: Wren Atelier
about: A small Filipino atelier that mixes Manila street food and local flowers with classic perfume materials.
why: Possibly the only perfume with a banana-cue (caramelized street banana) accord. Pure local storytelling.

sig.name: Manila Oud
sig.profile: Calamansi zest and ginger, then sampaguita (the Philippine jasmine) and a caramel-banana note, all sinking into smoky oud, leather and incense. Gourmand meets cathedral.

price.note: Sold through the Yuchengco Museum shop; size not listed.

name: GP Fragrances
about: A Filipino label whose 'Elements' series maps scents to places: Baguio, Banaue, Siargao, Mayon volcano.
why: A scent map of the Philippines; good material for the regional map project too.

sig.name: Baguio Verde
sig.profile: A cool morning in the mountain city of Baguio: pine, mist and crushed leaves over damp soil and vetiver. Green and outdoorsy.

price.note: Sold mainly through Instagram; no public price found.

name: Toouch
about: A new Vietnamese label (2025, perfumer Sy Truong) with one scent per city: Ho Chi Minh City, Da Nang, Hanoi.
why: Vietnam's perfume scene is just forming; this is a city-by-city scent portrait of the country.

sig.name: Smoky Graze (Ho Chi Minh City)
sig.profile: Saigon street coffee and cacao on warm amber. Its siblings: Dreamy Nautica (citrus and sea salt, Da Nang) and Heritage Nuzzle (green tea and soft woods, Hanoi).

name: Maison Bagian
about: Founded in 2018 by Hiệp Nguyễn and Alexandre Perucca: concepts developed in Vietnam, perfumes made in Grasse.
why: A French-Vietnamese bridge, with scents named Hanoian, Saigonaise and Mékong.

sig.name: Hanoian
sig.profile: A portrait of Hanoi; notes to be added after the next check.

name: Amouage
about: Oman's royal-born luxury house, famous for frankincense (Oman's ancient export) and grand, layered compositions.
why: Not untapped, but the benchmark for Gulf-style luxury: frankincense, oud and spice done with Western craftsmanship.

sig.name: Interlude Man
sig.profile: Smoky frankincense and leather with a herbal bite of oregano. Powerful and dramatic; a little goes a long way. (Notes from common listings.)

name: Abdul Samad Al Qurashi
city: Mecca origins; stores across the Gulf
about: A Saudi family house known for oud oils, bakhoor (scented wood chips to burn) and concentrated oil blends.
why: Real Gulf oud culture: oils dabbed on skin and clothes, often layered with a spray. A big step beyond 'oud' as a Western marketing word.

sig.name: Makkah Blend (perfume oil)
sig.profile: A dense, oily oud softened with flowers and musk. Intense and long-lasting; one dab is enough.

price.note: European reseller; sold out on the check date. 0.5 ml sample about US$8.90.

name: Swiss Arabian
about: A long-running Dubai perfume maker selling Arabian-style scents worldwide at low prices.
why: Affordable way to learn the Gulf palette (saffron, oud, rose, praline) before buying luxury.

sig.name: Shaghaf Oud
sig.profile: Saffron and rose over a sweet, nutty praline and soft oud. Warm, sweet and crowd-pleasing; a cold-weather scent.

name: Lattafa
about: The UAE brand behind the Arabian-perfume trend online, famous for rich sweet scents and for close alternatives to expensive designer and niche perfumes.
why: The trend you mentioned. Useful for Clay's 'expensive vs just as good' comparisons.

sig.name: Khamrah
sig.profile: Spiced dates and praline in a warm, boozy-feeling vanilla. Very sweet and very long-lasting; often compared to pricier boozy gourmands. (Notes from common listings.)

price.note: US distributor; size assumed from the standard 100 ml bottle.

name: Nishane
about: An Istanbul niche house drawing on Ottoman stories and Turkish shadow-puppet theatre, mostly in strong extrait concentration.
why: Shows how a non-Western house broke into global niche; the 15 ml size makes it easy to try.

sig.name: Hacivat (Extrait de Parfum)
sig.profile: Bright pineapple and bergamot over mossy, dry woods: a fresh, confident 'chypre' style that many compare to famous pineapple-birch scents.

price.note: Also sold in 50 ml and 100 ml.

name: Saint d'Ici (now Saint VII)
about: Natural, small-batch perfumes by Marie Aoun, made mostly from African materials bought from small farmers and craft distillers, including indigenous plants like buchu.
why: African indigenous botanicals (buchu, ouhout) are almost absent from global perfume. Each natural batch varies slightly year to year.

sig.name: Moussem
sig.profile: Cardamom and rose over aged, earthy vetiver and patchouli. Natural perfumes wear softer and closer to skin than synthetic ones. Also see Nsika, built on the mossy, camphor-like South African ouhout shrub.

price.note: Full bottles are 30 ml with 1 ml samples; current prices at saintvii.co.za.

name: Scentury Perfume & Co.
about: A South African maker of oil-based perfumes, many openly 'inspired by' famous designer scents, plus some original signatures.
why: Local, very affordable, and a clear example of the inspired-by market Clay will compare against originals.

sig.name: Vallée des Roses Oud (Extrait)
sig.profile: A rose-and-oud signature (floral, warm, spicy) in an oil-based extrait. Detailed notes not published.

price.note: Sale price; regular R549.90.

name: Beguile
about: A Nigerian fragrance house making strong, long-lasting perfumes priced for the local market, where big 100 ml bottles and powerful projection are preferred.
why: Nigeria has one of Africa's most passionate perfume cultures, and its own houses are just emerging.

sig.name: Blush Bloom
sig.profile: Almond and vanilla-orchid with creamy tuberose on a soft sandalwood base. Sweet, creamy and feminine. Their Sweet Oud pairs saffron and lavender with smoky oud.

price.note: Prices on their shop; not read on this pass.

name: XINÚ
about: A Mexican niche house built on native Mexican plants: copal, mesquite, vanilla, tobacco, agave and tropical leaves.
why: The clearest 'Mexico in a bottle' line; vanilla itself is native to Mexico.

sig.name: Copala
sig.profile: Copal is the sacred tree resin burned in Mexican ceremonies since Maya times: lemony, smoky, holy. Here it is warmed by mesquite and native vanilla. Powdery-smoky and soothing.

price.note: US retailer Luckyscent; samples available.

name: Coqui Coqui
about: A Yucatán perfumery-and-hotel brand making simple, single-idea scents from local plants.
why: Yucatán orange blossom is sweeter and less bitter than the European kind, a true terroir difference you can smell.

sig.name: Flor de Naranjo
sig.profile: Just orange blossom from Yucatán orange trees: honeyed, fresh and soft. Simple and sunny. Also try their Coco Coco and Tabaco.

name: Fueguia 1833
about: An Argentine house that works like a botanical expedition, using rare South American plants, plant-based musks and long maturing times.
why: Patagonian and Amazonian plants you won't find elsewhere, with clean-formula standards.

sig.name: Agua Magnoliana
sig.profile: A giant Amazonian magnolia tree in bloom: lemony-fresh magnolia petals over soft rosewood and the gentle, incense-like palo santo. Airy and luminous.

price.note: 30 ml $245, 100 ml $408 at the New York store.

name: Natura (Ekos)
about: Brazil's largest beauty brand. Its Ekos line uses Amazon materials (priprioca root, copaiba, pataqueira) sourced with forest communities.
why: Amazon raw materials at drugstore-ish prices, with sourcing stories you can check.

sig.name: Ekos Ryo Chuva
sig.profile: Rain falling on the Amazon: wet citrus, peppery green roots and leaves, then soft florals and a mossy wood base. Fresh and green.

price.note: US store price; size not shown on the page.

name: Zoologist Perfumes
about: A Toronto indie house where each perfume is an animal (Bat, Moth, Beaver, Tiger...), made with different guest perfumers.
why: Close to home, ships from Canada, and one of the most respected indie houses in the world.

sig.name: Deluxe bottles (e.g. Moth, Bat, Beaver)
sig.profile: Each animal is a different scent world, from powdery and soft (Moth) to dark, damp cave and fruit (Bat). Start with their sample sets.

price.note: Most deluxe bottles US$200, a few US$240; size not shown on the list page. Travel sprays and sample sets also sold.

name: Imaginary Authors
about: A US indie house where every scent comes with a made-up book or story.
why: Story-driven and affordable for niche; a contrast to the Asian houses' minimalism.

sig.name: A City on Fire
sig.profile: A struck match, smoke and dark berries over warm resin. Smoky but polished; an evening scent.

name: Goldfield & Banks
about: An Australian house built on native Australian plants and coastlines, with French perfumers.
why: Australian native botanicals (coastal moss, desert lime, sandalwood) are a whole palette most people never smell.

sig.name: Pacific Rock Moss
sig.profile: Sea spray on rocks: salty, herbal and lemony, with a clean cedar finish. Their best seller and a great summer scent.

price.note: Price shown for the default size, assumed 100 ml (50 and 10 ml also sold).

name: Hiram Green
about: A one-man indie house making all-natural perfumes by hand.
why: Proof that fully natural perfume can be rich and long-lasting; a great reference for Safe Batch's 'build from scratch' side.

sig.name: Moon Bloom
sig.profile: A tuberose stem cut fresh: green at first, then a creamy, spicy white-flower heart and a coconut-resin base. Lush and tropical.
